comment: Single source of truth for the web UI installer. One entry per deploy-all.sh layer key, in deploy order. 'nodes' maps to node ids in the architecture visualizer (index.html); an empty list means no dedicated node yet (rendered generically). 'why' is the plain-language explanation shown in the UI. Keep this in sync with deploy-all.sh component keys (a test enforces it).

layers.name: Shared VPC
layers.why: A private Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) with a NAT gateway. Only the voice-call runtime needs it, for outbound media to the Amazon Kinesis Video Streams (KVS) managed TURN relay.

layers.name: DynamoDB tables
layers.why: Amazon DynamoDB tables for customers, orders, menu, carts, and locations - the data the ordering tools read and write.

layers.name: Location Service
layers.why: Amazon Location Service for geocoding an address and finding the nearest restaurant.

layers.name: Ordering Lambdas
layers.why: AWS Lambda functions holding the ordering business logic (GetMenu, AddToCart, PlaceOrder, and the rest).

layers.name: Backend REST API
layers.why: An Amazon API Gateway REST API (AWS Identity and Access Management authorized) that fronts the ordering Lambdas.

layers.name: AgentCore Gateway (MCP tools)
layers.why: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway exposes the backend API as discoverable Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools the agents call by name.

layers.name: Shared AgentCore Memory
layers.why: One Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Memory resource keyed by a pseudonymous customer id, shared by all three runtimes so a customer is recognized across channels.

layers.name: Voice-call runtime (WebRTC)
layers.why: The Web Real-Time Communication (WebRTC) voice agent on AgentCore Runtime (Amazon Nova 2 Sonic), with media relayed through the KVS managed TURN relay.

layers.name: Voice-note runtime
layers.why: A bounded Amazon Nova 2 Sonic speech-to-speech runtime that turns an inbound voice note into a spoken reply (OGG Opus in, OGG Opus out).

layers.name: Chat runtime (multimodal text)
layers.why: The multimodal text runtime: Amazon Nova 2 Lite via the Bedrock Converse API, handling text, images, and documents.

layers.name: WhatsApp webhook + delivery
layers.why: The only public endpoint: an Amazon API Gateway webhook, an ingest Lambda that verifies and enqueues to Amazon SQS, a worker Lambda, a Sender Lambda for replies, the last-inbound window table, and the Secrets Manager containers for the Meta tokens.

layers.name: Order-status notifier
layers.why: Sends proactive order-status updates to the customer on WhatsApp as the order advances, with an optional demo kitchen simulator.
